newsitem.title: FINLAND: NERVOUS MARKKA SEEKS COMPASS AFTER FRENCH POLL.
newsitem.headline: NERVOUS MARKKA SEEKS COMPASS AFTER FRENCH POLL.

text.p: The markka firmed fractionally on Monday in the wake of Sunday's French Socialists' poll win, but forex dealers were very hard put to figure its direction.
Some saw weakening pressure on the German mark pointing to a narrow markka appreciation, but others said clearer pointers to an EMU delay would boost the mark.

"We have slightly adjusted our week's view to an appreciation of the Finnish markka," said Esko Torsti, economist at Enskilda, sighting DEM/FIM at 2.98-3.02 from a previous 3.00-3.03 outlook, mainly due to pressure on the German mark.

But trade was very nervous with operators hungry for a more solid pointer as to whether EMU would be delayed, or the euro weakened, as a result of the combination of the French socialist win and Germany's gold revaluation row.

One trader said it was easy to argue either way -- a delay in EMU might point to softening pressure on the markka but Finland's strong economic fundamentals could work to offset this. "I think we'll be very reactive," he said.
"The market doesn't actually know what's going to happen," said another trader. "People are watching for further clues."
All the German mark crosses would react quite sharply to more indications of an EMU delay, with the German mark set to appreciate, he said.
"In that case I think it's quite possible we will go and have a look at the mid-rate (DEM/FIM 3.04, where the markka was linked to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism)," he added.
Closer to home, traders said a possible Swedish "no" to early participation in EMU -- with news expected on Tuesday -- should already be largely priced in.
However they warned that even this, if combined with more solid euro-delay signals or indications the single currency would be weak, could fuel upheaval.
